results.problem: Dynamic approximately optimal binary search tree
results.quote: For any \(f\ge 1\) there exists a binary search tree T<sup>f</sup>, such that the depth of a leaf holding an element e<sub>i</sub> in T<sup>f</sup> does not exceed min(log(W/w<sub>i</sub>), log n)+O(f) and the amortized cost of updating T<sup>f</sup> after an element access or an insertion is O(log<sup>(f)</sup> n+f).

There is a binary alphabetic code C, such that (1) for t=0, ..., W-1 the codeword length of a symbol S[t+1]=a_i in C does not exceed min(log(t/w_i(t)), log n)+O(1) (2) the cost of encoding the next symbol, updating C after encoding a symbol or inserting a new symbol into C is O(1).
